metaTitle: Leaky Faucet Repair in Glendale, CA | Cost & Fix Guide
metaDescription: Fix a dripping faucet in Glendale for $135–$220. Learn common causes, what a plumber does, and whether it's a DIY job or not.
intro: That steady drip from your kitchen or bathroom faucet in Glendale isn't just annoying — it's wasting water and can stain sinks in older mid-century apartment buildings. Hillside homes with older plumbing lines often see this issue sooner due to mineral buildup and water pressure quirks common in the area.
causes: Worn-out rubber washers or O-rings inside the faucet body lose their seal over time.
Mineral deposits from Glendale's hard water can build up and prevent parts from closing fully.
A loose or corroded valve seat lets water seep past even when the faucet is off.
Cracked or degraded cartridges in newer faucets stop sealing properly.
High water pressure common in hillside properties can accelerate wear on internal parts.
whatProDoes: Shuts off the water supply to the fixture and inspects the faucet type and brand.
Disassembles the faucet handle and body to access the washer, cartridge, or valve seat.
Replaces worn washers, O-rings, or cartridges with matching parts.
Cleans or replaces the valve seat if corrosion or mineral buildup is found.
Reassembles the faucet, turns water back on, and checks for leaks under pressure.
Tests hot and cold sides separately to confirm the drip is fully resolved.
diyOrPro: If you're comfortable turning off the water supply and have the right size wrench, swapping a washer or O-ring on a simple faucet can be a reasonable DIY task. But older faucets in Glendale's mid-century buildings sometimes have corroded or hard-to-source parts, and forcing a stuck valve can crack pipes — at that point it's safer to call a plumber before a small drip becomes a bigger water issue.
priceNote: This job runs $135 to $220 in Glendale, based on a $94/hour rate for a typical 1-2 hour repair. The time varies depending on faucet type, whether parts need replacing, and how accessible the shut-off valve is in older homes.

faqs.q: Why does my faucet keep dripping even after I tighten the handle?
faqs.a: Tightening the handle harder won't fix a worn washer, cartridge, or valve seat — those parts need to be replaced, not just tightened, or the drip will continue.

faqs.q: Can a leaky faucet cause damage if I wait to fix it?
faqs.a: Yes, constant dripping can stain sinks, waste water, and in some cases lead to mineral buildup or corrosion around the fixture, especially with Glendale's hard water.

faqs.q: Do I need to replace the whole faucet or just a part inside it?
faqs.a: Most leaks are fixed by replacing an internal part like a washer, O-ring, or cartridge — a full faucet replacement is usually only needed if the fixture itself is cracked or very old.
